evidence: pyproject.toml:113 sets addopts = "--ignore=tests/connectors". Pytest's --ignore option values are turned into absolute paths relative to the current working directory (os.path.abspath in _pytest/main.py pytest_ignore_collect), not the rootdir. addopts are plain command-line args, so they get no rootdir resolution. From a cwd other than the repo root, e.g. running `pytest /repo` from elsewhere, the ignore resolves to <cwd>/tests/connectors and does not match, so the directory is collected. The claim 'regardless of the working directory' is therefore false. Only testpaths is rootdir-relative. This is from my knowledge of pytest, not an executed run.

I did not run pytest and did not read the pinned pytest version or the head pyproject.toml. The claim rests on how pytest's pytest_ignore_collect treats explicitly named paths. From memory, initial paths are exempt from ignore checks (the isinitpath check), so the claim is probably true. I did not verify this against the pinned version.

collection_state (src/sqllens/_memory_consistency.py:63-76) stats the directory and keys on (st_dev, st_ino, collection_name) in a lock-guarded WeakValueDictionary; distinct directories give distinct keys and aliases of one directory give the same key, so the same object. The test at tests/unit/test_memory_listing_consistency.py:238-250 asserts exactly this on both case-sensitive and case-insensitive filesystems, and holds the first state while evaluating the second, so weak refs do not break identity. A non-existent directory raises from stat(); the docstring says Chroma must create it first.

Test at tests/unit/test_memory_listing_consistency.py:238-250 branches on variant.exists() after creating only MixedCase. If it exists, the filesystem is case-insensitive and both spellings stat to the same (st_dev, st_ino), so collection_state (src/sqllens/_memory_consistency.py:69-76, keyed by dev/inode/name) returns the same object. Otherwise variant.mkdir() creates a distinct directory with a different inode and the states differ. Neither branch skips. A case-sensitive but normalizing filesystem would still hit exists() true with a shared inode, so the test holds there too.
